intro: The City of Light: boulevards, cafés, world-class museums and the Seine running through it all.
areas: Medieval lanes, boutiques, falafel and LGBTQ+ bars.
Cafés, bookshops and the Luxembourg Gardens.
sights: Home of the Mona Lisa (timed entry).
Impressionist masterpieces in a former station.
See the monuments from the water.
eat: Steak frites, confit de canard and onion soup.
night: Bars, clubs and live music in two of the liveliest districts.
Shows at Montmartre and the Champs-Élysées.
arrive: Charles de Gaulle (RER B or Roissybus) and Orly (Orlyval or Metro line 14) airports. Eurostar arrives at Gare du Nord.
around: Metro, RER, buses and trams; the centre is walkable.
pass: Navigo Easy card or Navigo Découverte weekly pass; contactless payment is rolling out. The Paris Museum Pass covers many sights.
tip: Many museums close one day a week (often Monday or Tuesday); check first.

intro: Canals, gabled houses, cycling and great museums, with a famous nightlife scene.
areas: World Heritage canals and the Nine Streets.
Creative venues across the IJ by free ferry.
sights: Rembrandt and the Dutch Golden Age.
The world’s largest Van Gogh collection (timed tickets).
night: Squares packed with clubs, bars and music venues.
arrive: Schiphol Airport has trains to Amsterdam Centraal (about 15–20 minutes). Eurostar arrives at Centraal.
around: Trams, Metro, buses and free ferries; cycling is everywhere.
pass: GVB day tickets or contactless OVpay; I amsterdam City Card includes transport and museums.
when: April–May for tulips; June–September for long days; King’s Day on 27 April.
tip: Stay out of bike lanes and look both ways for cyclists.

intro: A city of history and reinvention: the Wall, world-class museums and legendary techno.
areas: Brandenburg Gate, Museum Island and Unter den Linden.
Street food, bars and a multicultural mix.
Cafés and the Mauerpark flea market.
Clubs and the East Side Gallery.
sights: Book the Reichstag dome visit online (free).
World Heritage museums including the Pergamon.
Longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall.
Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe.
eat: Market hall with Thursday Street Food.
night: Famous venues with strict door policies.
arrive: Berlin Brandenburg Airport (BER) is linked by FEX airport express and S-Bahn. Hauptbahnhof has trains across Germany.
around: U-Bahn, S-Bahn, trams and buses run late; night services at weekends.
pass: AB-zone day tickets or the Berlin WelcomeCard; the Deutschlandticket for longer stays.
tip: Cash is still handy in some bars and clubs.

intro: The Eternal City: ancient ruins, Baroque piazzas and the Vatican, with food at every corner.
areas: Pantheon, Piazza Navona and the Trevi Fountain.
Boutiques and wine bars near the Forum.
St Peter’s and the Vatican Museums.
sights: Combined ticket with the Palatine (book ahead).
Ancient temple with a ticketed entry.
Throw a coin over your shoulder.
eat: Carbonara, cacio e pepe and amatriciana.
Morning food markets with fresh produce and street food.
arrive: Fiumicino Airport (Leonardo Express train or FL1) and Ciampino (bus). Roma Termini has high-speed trains.
around: Metro (lines A, B and C), buses and trams; the centre is best on foot.
pass: BIT single tickets, 24–72 hour passes or contactless; the Roma Pass adds museum entry.
tip: Cover shoulders and knees for churches; carry a refillable bottle for the street fountains (nasoni).

intro: A fairy-tale city of spires and bridges, with a castle, great beer and a famous astronomical clock.
areas: Old Town Square and the Astronomical Clock.
Local bars, cafés and beer gardens.
sights: One of the largest ancient castle complexes.
Medieval clock on the Old Town Hall.
eat: Beef in cream sauce with dumplings.
A tourist pastry; Czech classics are better.
arrive: Václav Havel Airport is linked by bus to the Metro and the Airport Express to the main station.
around: Metro, trams and buses; walkable centre.
pass: Short-term tickets and 24/72-hour passes via the PID Lítačka app.
when: April–June and September–October; December for Christmas markets.
tip: Use official exchange offices and pay in koruna, not euros.

intro: Imperial palaces, coffee houses and classical music in one of the world’s most liveable cities.
areas: St Stephen’s Cathedral and the Hofburg.
The Prater and its Giant Ferris Wheel.
sights: Standing-room tickets are a local tradition.
eat: Breaded veal escalope, Vienna’s signature dish.
Rich chocolate cake with apricot jam.
Wine taverns on the city edge.
night: Summer bars and beach bars along the canal.
arrive: Vienna Airport has the CAT express and S-Bahn trains. Wien Hauptbahnhof has trains across Europe.
around: U-Bahn, trams and buses; Wiener Linien runs a dense network.
pass: 24–72 hour tickets or the Vienna City Card; check current fares.
when: April–June and September–October; Advent markets in December.
tip: Order a Melange in a coffee house and stay as long as you like.

intro: Two cities across the Danube: thermal baths, grand architecture and the famous ruin bars.
areas: Castle, Fisherman’s Bastion and Matthias Church.
Ruin bars and the Great Synagogue.
sights: Outdoor thermal pools in City Park.
Best at night when the city is lit.
eat: Grand central market with food stalls upstairs.
night: Weekend night events at some thermal baths (check dates).
arrive: Budapest Airport is linked by the 100E airport bus. Keleti station has international trains.
around: Metro, trams and buses; tram 2 along the Danube is scenic.
pass: 24-hour to weekly travel cards; the Budapest Card adds attractions.
tip: Check menu prices and pay in forints; tip only if service is not included.

intro: The capital of the Riviera: a pebble beach, the Promenade des Anglais and a colourful old town.
areas: Old town lanes and the Cours Saleya market.
sights: Viewpoint over the Bay of Angels.
Works by Matisse in a villa in Cimiez.
eat: Local classics with tuna, egg and olives.
Onion tart with anchovies and olives.
night: Bars and restaurants around the harbour.
arrive: Nice Côte d’Azur Airport is linked by tram line 2. Nice-Ville station has trains along the coast.
around: Trams and Lignes d’Azur buses; walk the centre.
pass: Lignes d’Azur tickets and day passes; check current fares.
when: May–June and September; Carnival in February.
tip: Take the regional train to Villefranche-sur-Mer or Monaco.

intro: France’s food capital, with Renaissance lanes, traboules and two rivers.
areas: Between the rivers, with squares and shops.
eat: Light pike dumplings in a creamy sauce.
night: Bars on boats on the Rhône.
arrive: Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport has the Rhônexpress tram. Part-Dieu station has TGVs to Paris.
pass: TCL tickets and the Lyon City Card; check current fares.
when: April–June, September–October; December for the Fête des Lumières.

intro: France’s oldest city: a buzzing Old Port, the calanques and a proud multicultural spirit.
sights: Limestone coves by boat or on foot.
Island fortress from The Count of Monte Cristo.
arrive: Marseille Provence Airport is linked by shuttle bus. Saint-Charles station has TGVs to Paris.
around: Metro, trams and buses; ferries to the islands.
pass: RTM tickets and the City Pass; check current fares.
tip: Check calanques access rules in summer; some need a free reservation.

intro: The world’s wine capital, with an elegant riverside, World Heritage architecture and a great food scene.
sights: Place de la Bourse & Water Mirror
Immersive museum of world wine with a tasting deck.
night: Riverside bars along the Garonne quays.
arrive: Bordeaux-Mérignac Airport is linked by tram line A and shuttle bus. Saint-Jean station has TGVs to Paris (about 2 hours).
around: Trams and buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: TBM tickets and the Bordeaux CityPass; check current fares.
tip: Book vineyard tours in advance, especially in harvest season.

intro: La Ville Rose: pink-brick streets, aerospace heritage and a lively student city on the Garonne.
sights: Grand main square in front of the city hall.
eat: Coarse pork sausage, a regional staple.
night: Well-known concert venue south of the city.
arrive: Toulouse-Blagnac Airport is linked by shuttle bus and tram. Matabiau station has trains to Paris and Bordeaux.
pass: Tisséo tickets and passes; check current fares.
tip: Visit the Garonne quays at sunset when the bricks glow pink.

intro: Italy’s capital of fashion and design, with the Duomo, The Last Supper and aperitivo culture.
night: Aperitivo and bars along the canals.
Home of AC Milan and Inter.
arrive: Malpensa (Malpensa Express), Linate (Metro M4) and Bergamo (bus) airports. Milano Centrale has high-speed trains.
pass: ATM tickets, day passes or contactless; check current fares.
tip: Book The Last Supper well in advance; tickets sell out.

intro: Renaissance art and architecture, the Duomo and Tuscan food.
eat: Food hall above the San Lorenzo market.
arrive: Florence Airport is linked by tram T2; Pisa Airport has trains. Santa Maria Novella station has high-speed trains.
around: Walk; trams and buses for the outskirts.
pass: Autolinee Toscane tickets; check current options.
tip: Book museum tickets ahead to skip long queues.

intro: The city on water: canals, palaces and St Mark’s Basilica.
areas: St Mark’s Square and the Doge’s Palace.
Local bars and the Jewish Ghetto.
sights: Gothic palace of the Venetian Republic.
arrive: Marco Polo Airport is linked by bus and Alilaguna water bus. Santa Lucia station is on the Grand Canal.
around: Vaporetto water buses run the Grand Canal and lagoon; otherwise everything is on foot.
pass: ACTV travel cards (1–7 days); check current fares.
when: April–May and October; check day-tripper fee dates.
tip: Day-trippers may need to pay the access fee on certain dates; check before travelling.

intro: Vibrant, chaotic and delicious: the birthplace of pizza, with Vesuvius and Pompeii close by.
night: Aperitivo bars in an elegant seafront district.
arrive: Naples Airport is linked by Alibus. Napoli Centrale has high-speed trains; Circumvesuviana goes to Pompeii.
pass: Unico Campania tickets; check current fares.
tip: Visit Pompeii early and bring water and sun protection.

intro: ‘La Grassa’: porticoes, medieval towers and Italy’s richest food city.
eat: Tiny filled pasta in a rich broth.
night: Bohemian street of bars and osterie.
arrive: Bologna Airport is linked by the Marconi Express monorail. Bologna Centrale has high-speed trains.
around: Walk under the porticoes; TPER buses.
tip: Climb the Asinelli Tower (book ahead; check current access).

intro: An elegant Alpine-edge city of baroque squares, royal palaces, Egyptian treasures and chocolate.
areas: Multicultural district with Turin’s busiest nightlife.
sights: One of the world’s great Egyptian collections.
Cinema museum with a panoramic lift.
eat: Turin is the birthplace of vermouth; try it at aperitivo.
night: Bars and clubs around Largo Saluzzo.
arrive: Turin Airport is linked by train and bus. Porta Nuova and Porta Susa stations have high-speed trains.
pass: GTT tickets and the Torino+Piemonte Card; check current options.
tip: Try a bicerin at a historic café.
